newsitem.title: FINLAND: ERICSSON H1 BOOSTS NOKIA EXPECTATIONS.
newsitem.headline: ERICSSON H1 BOOSTS NOKIA EXPECTATIONS.

text.p: Expectations for Nokia's second quarter earnings were boosted on Thursday as Swedish Ericsson reported its mobile phone sales doubled in the first half and beat earnings forecasts clearly, analysts said.

Nokia had previously been expected to show lower mobile phones sales growth than in the first quarter, but Ericsson's report sparked hopes that second quarter growth would be closer to the 58 percent reached in the first, they said.
"I had been looking for 40 to 50, now I expect 50 to 60 percent," said FIM Securities analyst Niklas Geust.
Nokia's first half interim report is due Monday, August 4.
In the first quarter, Nokia's Mobile Phone arm had net sales of 6.15 billion markka -- up from 3.89 billion markka a year earlier -- and Nokia said profitability was very good.

Ericsson's report was hailed, partly because of the strength of cellular phones growth, but also because it beat the consensus forecast by some 20 percent. Ericsson's first half pretax profit was 6.1 billion crowns, while the average forecast was for a 5.11 billion crown profit.
A key question in Nokia's report would be to see whether it has been losing market share to Ericsson, though analysts said they would also focus on Nokia's comments about sales of new models.

"As such the market share in one quarter is not important, but in this situation, people will be very quickly trying to pick up trends from the data," said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell analyst Johan Strandberg in Stockholm.

Nokia's share jumped on Ericsson's report, trading some five percent or 21 markka higher at 446.00 at 1600/1300 GMT as the market discounted good growth news from Nokia as well, but some analysts saw volatility next week.
"I think it was alright for the share to rise, but it will get nervous towards the end of next week," said FIM's Geust.
